content.question_text: What is the name of the JDK utility tool that generates HTML documentation from your source files?
What special delimiter must a comment start with to be recognized as a documentation comment by the utility tool?
What are the five specific code items that the javadoc utility extracts information for?

core_requirements: Public and protected constructors and methods

content.question_text: Where exactly must a documentation comment be placed in relation to the member it describes?
What is the special significance of the very first sentence in a documentation comment's free-form text?

core_requirements: It acts as a summary statement.
The javadoc utility automatically extracts these first sentences to generate summary pages.
acceptable_variations: It is extracted for the summary section.

content.question_text: What is the structural difference between a block tag and an inline tag in a documentation comment?

core_requirements: Block tags must appear at the beginning of a line (starting with @).
Inline tags are enclosed in braces (e.g., {@tagname}) and can be placed anywhere in the text.
acceptable_variations: Block tags start a line, inline tags use curly braces inside the text.

content.question_text: Starting with Java 23, what alternative syntax format can you use to author JavaDoc comments instead of plain text and HTML?
What is the delimiter required to denote a Markdown documentation comment?
Where specifically must a class comment be placed within a Java file?

core_requirements: After any import statements and directly before the class definition.
acceptable_variations: Between the imports and the class declaration.

content.question_text: Is it strictly required to add an asterisk (*) at the front of every line inside a multi-line /** ... */ comment?

acceptable_variations: No, but IDEs usually add them automatically.

content.question_text: Write the exact tag used to add an entry to the "parameters" section of a method.
Write the exact tag used to add a "returns" section to the current method.
Write the exact tag used to add a note that a method may throw an exception.
What tag allows you to copy the documentation verbatim from a method in a superclass or interface?
While you only need to document public fields, what specific type of fields does this generally apply to in practice?
To generate package-level comments, you cannot put them in a standard Java class file. What are the two files you can create to supply these comments?
If you want to type monospaced code in your documentation without having to manually escape HTML characters like `<` and `&`, what inline tag should you use?
What block tag adds a hyperlink to the "see also" section of the documentation?
When linking to a specific method using the `@see` or `{@link}` tags, what character must you use to separate the class name from the method name?
If you want to place a hyperlink to another class or method inline anywhere within your comment text (rather than in the "see also" section), what tag must you use?
Name the three general block tags used to document the author, the current version, and the version a feature was introduced in.
Introduced in Java 18, what tag allows you to import code from external files to minimize the risk of stale or incorrect documentation snippets?
What happens if you omit the `-d docDirectory` option when running the javadoc command in your terminal?

core_requirements: The generated HTML files are extracted directly into the current directory (which gets very messy).
acceptable_variations: It dumps all the files into your current working folder.
